# 0.6.0 — First-run fixes after 0.5.0

23 September 2026. Minor on **0.5.0**.

Upgrade if a command checked the wrong directory, hid what `--json` already showed, or crashed on a repository that was not finished yet. A few JSON fields and exit results change, so read **Changed** before upgrading a pipeline.

## Install

```bash
pip install opentide==0.6.0
export OPENTIDE_REPO_ROOT=/path/to/detection-repo
opentide validate --strict
```

If you generated CI with `opentide setup ci`, regenerate it so `--default-branch` matches the branch you deploy from: `opentide setup ci <github|gitlab|azure> --yes`.

## Changed

- `validate --json` names the directory it read under `workspace`. A full run that finds no objects still exits `0`, and its message names that directory ([#294](https://github.com/OpenTideHQ/opentide/issues/294)).
- `setup mcp --generic` returns its copy-the-file instruction as `advice` instead of `note` ([#292](https://github.com/OpenTideHQ/opentide/issues/292)).
- SDK: the registry index has a `file_paths` map. `ValidationScope.path_basenames` is removed; a path target matches only the object's own file ([#297](https://github.com/OpenTideHQ/opentide/issues/297)).
- An unset Splunk `frequency_scheduling` keeps the mode it deployed with before: `current` for a legacy `[setup]` table, `random` for a `[[tenants]]` entry ([#295](https://github.com/OpenTideHQ/opentide/issues/295)).

## Fixed

- Commands find a detection workspace from `.opentide/` or `objects/`, including one nested in a larger git checkout. `validate --strict` no longer passes having checked nothing ([#294](https://github.com/OpenTideHQ/opentide/issues/294)).
- `validate --file` matches that path only. Issues name the object's own file, and `rule.file` points at it ([#297](https://github.com/OpenTideHQ/opentide/issues/297)).
- Human output keeps bracketed text (`[deploy, validate]`, `[error]`, `opentide[sentinel]`), prints `advice` and `detail`, lists lint findings, and `info rules` / `threats` / `objectives` / `coverage` print the section you asked for ([#292](https://github.com/OpenTideHQ/opentide/issues/292), [#293](https://github.com/OpenTideHQ/opentide/issues/293)).
- `rule.metadata.schema` returns `"rule::1.0"`, not Pydantic's `BaseModel.schema` ([#298](https://github.com/OpenTideHQ/opentide/issues/298)).
- `generate docs` writes an actor's stage as `att&ck`, not `('att&ck',)` ([#296](https://github.com/OpenTideHQ/opentide/issues/296)).
- `info` no longer logs a Splunk frequency warning for a repository that does not use Splunk ([#295](https://github.com/OpenTideHQ/opentide/issues/295)).
- `deploy` in a repository without `objects/rules/` reports `skipped` (exit `0`) instead of `Errno 2`. Rule files in subfolders are still not deployed; the plan names them in a warning ([#300](https://github.com/OpenTideHQ/opentide/issues/300), [#312](https://github.com/OpenTideHQ/opentide/issues/312)).
- An enabled platform with no `[[tenants]]` entry fails `deploy` and `validate query --live` with the file to edit, before any engine loads. `--dry-run` previews payloads and warns ([#314](https://github.com/OpenTideHQ/opentide/issues/314)).
- `setup --ci` accepts `--default-branch` and prints the same warnings as `setup ci` ([#288](https://github.com/OpenTideHQ/opentide/issues/288), [#308](https://github.com/OpenTideHQ/opentide/issues/308)).
- `--no-promotion` and `--promotion-target` write `[promotion]` in `.opentide/configurations/deployment.toml`. Omitting them keeps the repository's setting; an explicit flag that disagrees with an existing table exits `2` ([#307](https://github.com/OpenTideHQ/opentide/issues/307)).
- Documented CLI samples for deploy, troubleshooting, and the tutorial match what the commands print ([#299](https://github.com/OpenTideHQ/opentide/issues/299)).
- `vocab-upstream.yml` parses again, so the vocabulary drift gate runs ([#287](https://github.com/OpenTideHQ/opentide/issues/287)). `publish-pypi.yml` can be retried after a PyPI 5xx without uploading a file twice ([#289](https://github.com/OpenTideHQ/opentide/issues/289)).

## Tests

Each fix has a regression for the reported case and a guard for the class: human output against `--json`, workspace discovery from subdirectories, `--file` against same-basename twins, documented output samples run as the CLI, and a tenantless scaffold for every platform.

## Verify

```bash
python -c "import opentide; print(opentide.__version__)"
opentide setup --yes --name "Tutorial Detections" --org "Example Corp" --platform sentinel --path /tmp/tutorial-detections
opentide --repo /tmp/tutorial-detections validate --strict
```

Expect `0.6.0`.
